title: Marta Roig Quartet
why: Explore Marta Roig Quartet at Jamboree, Plaça Reial.

title: In the Mood for Love
why: Explore In the Mood for Love at Filmoteca de Catalunya, Raval.

title: Trio Carioca
why: Seven-string guitar, pandeiro and flute in a room for about eighty people.

title: Orquesta La Clave
why: Explore Orquesta La Clave at Sala Apolo, Poble-sec.

title: The Quiet Season
why: Explore The Quiet Season at Cinemes Verdi, Gràcia.

title: Laia Serra Trio
why: Piano trio playing Mompou and Monk side by side.

title: Nit de bossa nova
why: Explore Nit de bossa nova at Mas de les Vinyes, Palafrugell.

title: The Quiet Season
why: Explore The Quiet Season at Cinema Truffaut, Girona.

title: Congost de Mont-rebei
why: Cliffside path through the gorge of the Noguera Ribagorçana; check access and parking before visiting.
context: The Noguera Ribagorçana cuts through the Montsec, and a trail carved into the rock follows the gorge above the water. Check the access notice and La Masieta parking calendar before setting out, and book a parking space in advance.

title: Ullastret Iberian town
why: The largest Iberian settlement in Catalonia: walls and streets on a hilltop, with a small museum.
context: Puig de Sant Andreu was a capital of the Indigetes, with walls, houses, cisterns and a museum of finds from the site. Check seasonal opening hours before visiting and pair it with nearby Peratallada.

title: Indians museum, Begur
why: The story of Begur’s emigrants to the Americas and their architectural legacy.
context: The centre explores the legacy of Catalans who crossed the Atlantic in search of fortune, including many people from Begur in the 19th century. Follow the free audio-guided route past the town’s indiano houses afterwards.

title: Bell-lloc winery
why: Underground winery designed by RCR Arquitectes, with tastings among the vines.
context: RCR Arquitectes set this cellar into the landscape of a working estate near Palamós. Arrange a visit for a tour and tasting of the estate’s wines and other produce.

title: Masia Serra
why: Family winery in the Albera hills above Cantallops.
context: This family winery sits among vines and olive trees in the Albera and makes Empordà wines. Book ahead for a tasting, with options that include food or a picnic among the vines.

title: Mas Estela
why: Organic winery in the hills behind La Selva de Mar, near Cap de Creus.
context: The Soto-Dalmau family restored this estate in the Sant Romà valley, inside the Cap de Creus natural park, and farms its vines organically and biodynamically. Arrange a visit in advance to see the estate and taste its wines.

title: Arché Pagès
why: Small family winery in Capmany, in the heart of Empordà wine country.
context: The fourth generation of the Arché Pagès winegrowing family founded its own cellar in Capmany in 2004. The Empordà wine route lists cellar visits with a tasting; contact the winery to arrange one.

title: Douglas DC-6 memorial
why: Memorial to a Douglas DC-6 that crashed near Cantallops in 1986.
context: The remains and a plaque commemorate four crew members who died when a French firefighting aircraft crashed in the Albera in 1986. Masia Serra, also on this list, is in Cantallops and can make a second stop in the area.

title: Terracotta ceramics museum
why: La Bisbal’s pottery tradition, shown in an old ceramics factory.
context: The museum occupies a former ceramic factory in La Bisbal, where production continued until 1984. Its collection and exhibitions introduce the town’s pottery tradition; check ahead for guided visits and workshops.

title: Balneari Vichy Catalan
why: Historic spa hotel in Caldes de Malavella – thermal baths for the day.
context: This historic spa grew around the thermal springs that gave Vichy Catalan its name. Check the spa’s current day-visit options and reserve a thermal circuit before travelling.

title: Mas Falgarona
why: Restored 17th-century farmhouse with a fine restaurant near Figueres.
context: A farmhouse hotel and spa in Avinyonet de Puigventós, near Figueres, Mas Falgarona also has a restaurant serving local produce. Check restaurant and spa availability before making it a day trip.

title: Les Cols Pavellons
why: RCR Arquitectes’ glass pavilions next to Les Cols, Fina Puigdevall’s restaurant in Olot.
context: RCR Arquitectes designed these glass pavilions beside the Les Cols farmhouse and restaurant in Olot. They are accommodation rather than an open architectural exhibition, so arrange a stay or meal ahead of time.

title: Mas d'en Roqueta
why: Country hotel near La Seu d’Urgell, with views toward the Cadí.
context: This country hotel in Aravell looks toward the Cadí range and offers rooms and a converted barn for stays. Check directly about meals before visiting; the current hotel site does not describe a restaurant.

title: Xic's Cal Borrech
why: Family wine and olive-oil producer in the Pallars Jussà; arrange a visit in advance.
context: This family producer grows vines and olives in the Pallars Jussà and offers vineyard visits and tastings. Sources differ on the restaurant’s status, so contact the producer to confirm current options and arrange a visit.

title: Masia el Puig
why: Rural lodging in the Vall de Bianya, in the Garrotxa.
context: This rural lodging is at El Puig de Castellar de la Muntanya in the Vall de Bianya. Contact the property before visiting and consider pairing a stay with a trip to Castellfollit de la Roca.

title: Hostal la Placeta
why: Camprodon inn on Plaça del Carme, home to the Cal Marquès restaurant.
context: This inn on Camprodon’s Plaça del Carme now shares its home with the Cal Marquès restaurant. Book a meal or room ahead and leave time to walk over the town’s Pont Nou.

title: Hotel Mas de Xaxas
why: Small hotel by the river in Camprodon.
context: Mas de Xaxàs occupies a late-19th-century house recognised as part of Camprodon’s historic heritage. Its terrace looks toward the river and mountains; check availability before planning a meal or stay.

title: Hotelet del Bac
why: Hotel with valley views just outside Camprodon.
context: This small rural hotel overlooks the Camprodon valley and serves breakfasts made with local products. Meals are by reservation, so check with the hotel before making a special trip.

title: Hotel Cal Rei de Talló
why: Stone hotel in the Cerdanya near Bellver.
context: Set in a former hay barn in the village of Talló, this small hotel has a restaurant focused on local and seasonal ingredients. Check the restaurant’s opening days and pair a visit with Prullans across the Cerdanya valley.

title: Hostal El Forn de Beget
why: Historic family inn and restaurant in the stone village of Beget.
context: This family-run inn and restaurant occupies a building recorded as an inn in 1586. Pair a meal with a walk through Beget to the Romanesque church of Sant Cristòfol.

title: Aquàrium de Barcelona
why: Mediterranean and tropical tanks, with a walk-through shark tunnel.
context: The aquarium’s exhibits range from Mediterranean habitats to tropical seas, with a transparent tunnel through the main shark tank. Check feeding times and book tickets online before visiting.

title: Camprodon
why: Pyrenean town known for its medieval Pont Nou over the Ter.
context: The Pont Nou crosses the Ter just below its meeting with the Ritort and has been rebuilt over the centuries. Walk through the old town and pair the visit with Beget or a meal at Hostal La Placeta.

title: Castelnou
why: Hilltop medieval village in French Catalonia, one of the “plus beaux villages de France”.
context: This fortified village in French Catalonia climbs toward a medieval castle, with views toward Canigou. Park below the village and explore its steep, cobbled lanes on foot.

title: Castellbell i el Vilar
why: Small town on the Llobregat at the foot of Montserrat.
context: The Llobregat winds through this Bages municipality below Montserrat. Its medieval Pont Vell crosses the river beneath the castle, with views toward the mountain.

title: L'Astor
why: Tiny hilltop hamlet in the Anoia with wide views.
context: This small hamlet in Pujalt keeps a medieval street plan with covered passages and stone arches. Pair it with Argençola for a tour of the Anoia uplands.

title: Fonollosa
why: Quiet farming village in the Bages.
context: Fonollosa is a rural Bages municipality made up of several settlements among fields and woods. Explore the countryside and the medieval towers of Fals in the same municipality.

title: Argençola
why: Hilltop village in the Anoia uplands.
context: The remains of an 11th-century castle crown this village in the Anoia uplands. The local tourism office suggests a short walk to the old ice well; access to the castle itself is restricted.

title: Prullans
why: Cerdanya village on a sunny slope facing the Cadí.
context: This Cerdanya village faces the Cadí mountains across the valley. Look for the Romanesque church of Sant Esteve, then explore the viewpoints on the walking route toward Ardòvol.

title: Solsona
why: Cathedral town with a well-kept old quarter.
context: The old town retains three gates in its former walls and a Gothic cathedral with a Romanesque image of the Mare de Déu del Claustre. A guided old-town walk also takes in the squares and the town’s festival giants.

title: Talamanca
why: Medieval village around a castle above the Talamanca stream.
context: Talamanca grew around a castle whose present structure was rebuilt after the War of the Spanish Succession. Pair a walk through its old streets with nearby Mura, another village on this list.

title: Santa Coloma de Cervelló
why: Home of Gaudí’s crypt at the Colònia Güell.
context: The Colònia Güell is a former textile workers’ settlement with an unfinished church by Antoni Gaudí. Visit the crypt and walk the residential streets of the colony; check entry times ahead.

title: Granera
why: Tiny village in the Moianès with a castle and a Romanesque church.
context: Granera’s small settlements grew around a medieval castle in the Moianès. Walk up toward the castle remains and look for the Romanesque church of Santa Cecília.

title: Olivella
why: Village in the Garraf hills, close to Sitges.
context: Olivella is an inland Garraf village within reach of the Garraf park’s walking routes. Combine a stroll through the village with time in the surrounding limestone hills.

title: Sant Llorenç de la Muga
why: Walled medieval village on the Muga river.
context: The old village retains walls, towers and gateways beside the Muga. Follow the river to the old bridges, then explore the lanes inside the walls.

title: Tortosa
why: Historic city on the Ebre with a Gothic cathedral and the Suda castle.
context: Tortosa’s old quarter sits below the Suda castle on the Ebre. Walk from the Gothic cathedral to the Renaissance courtyard of the Reials Col·legis and up to the castle viewpoint.

title: Benifallet
why: Ebre river village with show caves.
context: This village beside the Ebre is a base for visiting the Coves Meravelles and travelling on the river. Ask the tourism office about cave visits and pair the stop with nearby Tortosa.

title: Altafulla
why: Walled old town above the beach, near Tarragona.
context: The Vila Closa is Altafulla’s walled historic centre, below its castle and above the coast. Ask the tourism office about a guided walk, then head down to the beach.

title: La Vilella Baixa
why: Priorat village of tall houses stacked above the river.
context: The steep slope makes the village’s houses look several storeys taller from the river than from the street. Cross the three-arched bridge and find the dead-end Carrer que No Passa in the old quarter.

title: Queralbs
why: Stone mountain village on the Vall de Núria rack railway.
context: This mountain village is a stop on the rack railway to Vall de Núria. Leave time to explore the stone streets before taking the train up the valley.

title: Tavertet
why: Cliff-top village with views over the Sau reservoir.
context: Tavertet stands above the cliffs of the Collsacabra, overlooking the Sau valley. Pair the village and its viewpoints with Rupit, another stone village on the same plateau.

title: Monells
why: Arcaded medieval square in the Baix Empordà.
context: The arcaded Plaça Jaume I was once the site of an important medieval market. Wander the old streets, then pair the village with nearby Peratallada.

title: Rivert
why: Remote hamlet in the Pallars Jussà.
context: Rivert sits beneath a wall of rock in the Pallars Jussà, with springs, a pond and an old mill shaped by the village’s water. Walk through its two parts and look for the Romanesque church of Sant Martí.

title: Tivenys
why: Ebre river village among olive groves.
context: Tivenys lies on the Ebre between the river and its irrigation canal. Its municipal park is a place to pause by the water; pair the visit with Tortosa or Benifallet.

title: Taüll
why: Romanesque churches of the Vall de Boí, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
context: Sant Climent and Santa Maria are two of the Vall de Boí’s UNESCO-listed Romanesque churches. See the painting projection at Sant Climent and check church opening times before travelling.

title: Beget
why: Stone village in a deep valley with a Romanesque church.
context: Stone houses and bridges cluster around the streams in this Alta Garrotxa village. The Romanesque church of Sant Cristòfol holds the carved Majestat de Beget; check opening times and pair the visit with Hostal El Forn.

title: Prades
why: The “red village” of the Prades mountains, built of red sandstone.
context: Red sandstone gives Prades its nickname, the red village. Walk around the arcaded Plaça Major and its round fountain, then follow one of the marked routes into the surrounding mountains.

title: Montsonís
why: Hilltop village with a castle in the Noguera.
context: A castle crowns this small Noguera village, with a keep and rooms that can be visited on a guided tour. Check tour times and reserve ahead for the slots that require it.

title: Rupit
why: Stone village in the Collsacabra with a hanging footbridge.
context: A hanging footbridge leads into Rupit’s stone streets in the Collsacabra. Pair the village with Tavertet, or follow the local path toward the Sallent waterfall.

title: Castellar de n'Hug
why: Mountain village near the source of the Llobregat and the Asland cement museum.
context: The Llobregat rises near this Berguedà mountain village, and the former Asland cement factory is now a museum. Check the museum’s opening times and leave time for the walk to the river’s springs.

title: Santa Pau
why: Medieval village in the Garrotxa volcanic park.
context: Santa Pau’s medieval centre lies within the Garrotxa volcanic zone, close to the Croscat volcano. Explore the arcaded square and pair the village with a walk in the natural park.

title: Castellfollit de la Roca
why: Village perched on the edge of a basalt cliff.
context: The old village stands on a basalt cliff formed by overlapping lava flows. A marked circular walk descends to the Fluvià for a view back up at the cliff and returns through the old streets.

title: Peralada
why: Castle town known for its wine cellars and summer music festival.
context: Peralada combines a historic centre with a castle, a wine tradition and a summer music festival. Check the festival programme or cellar visit times before planning a trip.

title: Tivissa
why: Ribera d’Ebre village near the Iberian site of Castellet de Banyoles.
context: Tivissa’s old quarter has narrow streets around the church of Sant Jaume. The Iberian site of Castellet de Banyoles lies a few kilometres away and can be visited freely; guided visits are available by reservation.

title: Tossa de Mar
why: Walled old town on a headland above the beach.
context: The Vila Vella’s fortified walls and towers stand above Tossa’s beach. Walk through the gateway and old streets, and check for any access changes during restoration work.

title: Begur
why: Hilltop town with a castle, indiano houses and coves below.
context: A castle overlooks Begur’s old streets and the coves below. Pair a walk through town with the Indians interpretation centre and its audio-guided route past indiano houses.

title: Besalú
why: Romanesque bridge and a medieval Jewish quarter.
context: Besalú’s medieval bridge leads into an old town with a former Jewish quarter and ritual bath, or mikveh. Ask the tourism office about guided visits to the Jewish heritage sites.

photo.alt: The medieval bridge over the Fluvià at Besalú

title: Mura
why: Stone village in the Sant Llorenç del Munt park.
context: This Bages village is a gateway to Sant Llorenç del Munt i l’Obac Natural Park. Explore the old centre and the church of Sant Martí, then pair it with nearby Talamanca.

title: Peratallada
why: Walled medieval village with a moat cut into the rock.
context: The village’s medieval defences include a deep moat cut into the sandstone, walls and towers. Walk through the Portal de la Verge and around Plaça de les Voltes, then pair the trip with Monells.

photo.alt: Stone buildings in the fortified village of Peratallada

title: Gósol
why: Pyrenean village where Picasso spent the summer of 1906.
context: Picasso spent part of 1906 in this mountain village near Pedraforca, producing works inspired by its people and landscape. The local Picasso centre presents his Gósol period; check opening times before visiting.

title: Bagergue
why: The highest inhabited village in the Val d’Aran.
context: The highest inhabited village in the Val d’Aran has stone houses and the Romanesque church of Sant Fèlix. The Eth Corrau museum presents objects from traditional Aranese life; check its opening times before visiting.

title: Muntanya de Sal, Cardona
why: Guided walk inside a mountain of salt, then the castle above the town.
context: A guided walk enters a former salt mine to see folded layers and mineral formations. Book ahead and arrive early for the tour; Cardona’s castle and old town make a natural second stop.

title: Museu del Cinema
why: Shadow theatre, optical toys and early moving images from the Tomàs Mallol collection.
context: Follow the experiments that led to cinema in the former Casa de les Aigües. Sundays close at 14:00; the first Sunday of each month is free.

title: The Cult of Beauty
why: How beauty standards are made – through medicine, commerce, race and gender.
context: A Wellcome Collection project adapted for Barcelona, bringing historical objects and contemporary art into a critical look at bodies and exclusion. Tue–Sun 10:00–20:00; free Sunday afternoons require booking.

title: Charlotte Perriand. Free to Rethink the World
why: Furniture and exhibition design as a way to rethink everyday life, from a pioneering woman of modernism.
context: The show follows Perriand’s own creative voice, her exhibition designs and her connections with Sert, Miró, Picasso, Léger and Calder. Check admission options; weekend guided tours are sold separately with museum admission.

title: Anselm Kiefer. The Secret Life of Plants
why: Memory, mythology and science explored through lead, roots, books and monumental vitrines.
context: The Grothe Collection exhibition brings together Kiefer’s paintings, sculptures and artist’s books, including the Opus Magnum vitrines. Daily 10:00–19:30; closed 25 December.

title: Dana Lixenberg. American Images
why: Patient documentary portraits of American communities, beyond celebrity and familiar stereotypes.
context: Includes the long-running Imperial Courts project in Los Angeles, homelessness in Indiana and an Iñupiaq community in Alaska. Tue–Sun 11:00–19:00; non-holiday Tuesdays are free.

title: Concha Ibáñez. The Evocation of Landscape
why: Landscapes reconstructed from travel and memory, with a different restrained palette for each place.
context: Curated by Elina Norandi for the centenary of Ibáñez’s birth. Her studio paintings grew from travel sketches and photographs rather than painting outdoors. Included with museum admission; closed Mondays.

title: Instruments of the Soul
why: Medieval objects as mediators between everyday life and the sacred – an archaeology and anthropology crossover.
context: Matter and Spirit in Medieval Catalonia follows relics, textiles, sculpture, parchment and rock crystal through their original spiritual functions. Included with museum admission; closed Mondays.
